title: 2026 decarbonisation-readiness permit QA controls

sources.title: Decarbonisation readiness in environmental permit applications
Decarbonisation readiness in environmental permit applications

facts.source_fact: Decarbonisation-readiness guidance applies in England; carbon-capture-readiness requirements continue in Wales.
facts.expected_handling: Apply jurisdiction before readiness assessment.

facts.source_fact: The guidance applies to relevant environmental permit applications submitted on or after 28 February 2026.
facts.expected_handling: Use application date to select the readiness regime.

facts.source_fact: The requirements target new and substantially refurbished electricity-generating combustion power plants.
facts.expected_handling: Do not apply the requirement to unchanged existing plant without a supporting trigger.

facts.source_fact: A generator is substantially refurbished when refurbishment cost of combustion plant exceeds 50% of comparable new combustion-plant investment cost, excluding abatement plant.
facts.expected_handling: Require the statutory cost test before classifying refurbishment as substantial.

facts.source_fact: Requirements apply only to new capacity or substantially refurbished elements of a combustion power plant.
facts.expected_handling: Scope the assessment to the affected plant elements.

facts.source_fact: Fossil-fuel combustion power plants including CHP can be in scope.
facts.expected_handling: Include CHP when the statutory applicability conditions are met.

facts.source_fact: Biomass, biofuel and biogas combustion power plants can be in scope, including biogas or biomethane from anaerobic digestion.
facts.expected_handling: Do not assume biogenic fuel automatically removes readiness obligations.

facts.source_fact: Energy-from-waste plants generating electricity can be in scope, including permitted incinerators using gasification or pyrolysis-derived fuels.
facts.expected_handling: Apply waste-incineration scope rules before readiness classification.

facts.source_fact: Plants already burning hydrogen, capturing CO2 or using blends of low-carbon fuels with methane or natural gas can remain in scope.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat partial low-carbon operation as an automatic exemption.

facts.source_fact: Multiple smaller units at the same regulated facility may be considered together and can trigger readiness when total rated thermal input reaches 50 MWth or more.
facts.expected_handling: Aggregate technically connected same-facility units where required.

facts.source_fact: Existing combustion power plant is not required to demonstrate readiness until it undergoes substantial refurbishment.
facts.expected_handling: Keep unchanged existing plant outside the readiness gate.

facts.source_fact: New plant below 1 MWth can be outside scope where it is not part of another permitted installation and does not participate in capacity-market or balancing-services arrangements.
facts.expected_handling: Apply all exemption conditions before excluding sub-1-MW plant.

facts.source_fact: Combustion power plant burning gas generated from landfill waste only is listed among systems not required to demonstrate readiness.
facts.expected_handling: Require exact fuel-source match for the exemption.

facts.source_fact: Combustion power plant with a nuclear safety role under a nuclear site licence is listed as exempt.
facts.expected_handling: Require nuclear-licence safety-role evidence.

facts.source_fact: Certain 1 to 50 MWth emergency back-up plant used only for on-site emergency power and testing no more than 50 hours per year is exempt.
facts.expected_handling: Require emergency-use and annual-hours evidence.

facts.source_fact: An operator must demonstrate either readiness for a qualifying complete CCS system or readiness to convert to hydrogen as the primary fuel.
facts.expected_handling: Select and document a primary readiness route.

facts.source_fact: The qualifying complete CCS route requires capability for continuous operation at a minimum 90% capture rate.
facts.expected_handling: Use 90% as the minimum capture-readiness design criterion for this route.

facts.source_fact: Readiness assessment uses four tests: space, technical feasibility, transport/storage or hydrogen-fuel access, and economic feasibility.
facts.expected_handling: Require all four test categories for the chosen route.

facts.source_fact: The guidance does not impose fixed feasibility benchmarks; the operator must demonstrate no known barriers to future decarbonisation.
facts.expected_handling: Assess evidence against the no-known-barriers objective rather than inventing fixed thresholds.

facts.source_fact: Planning permission and environmental permitting are separate decisions with different purposes.
facts.expected_handling: Do not substitute planning approval for environmental-permit readiness evidence.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the cited source fact without broadening its scope.
Attach jurisdiction, application date, plant status and capacity before applying readiness rules.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents applying readiness requirements to out-of-scope plant.

guard_patterns.handling: Carry chosen decarbonisation route and all required test categories.
Carry source URL, publisher and guidance version into outputs.
Do not convert readiness rules into parcel-level measured emissions without a separate parcel-binding gate.
